originalPreBoundary:
I was on a six-month contract. My team lead, Mira, wrote the recommendation that would decide whether I stayed.

I had spent six weeks building the forecast she was about to present.

At my desk, I opened her slide deck on the desk display. The title said “Mira’s forecast.”

Yesterday I had asked about credit. She said, “Let me lead this one. I’ll mention your work.”

My own printed summary was with me at the desk. I walked to the meeting room with it.

The director looked at the title slide and said, “Mira, this could become our board proposal.”

Mira began showing the figures. I recognized the change I had made the previous evening. I hadn’t heard my name.

Before questions, we had a short break. I stepped into the hallway. Mira and the director stayed in the meeting room; the door was open.

I could return to the room and step into the hallway again during the break. When the meeting resumed, I could go back to my seat or stand nearer the director.

I looked at my summary, with my name at the top. Below it was the revision I recognized on the screen.

When I returned and the meeting resumed, the director asked, “Anything to add before we use this?”

I could speak to the room then, ask the director now that we clarify the credit privately after the meeting, or let this question pass without speaking. I didn’t know whether Mira would still mention me or how she would write my recommendation if I challenged the credit.

I was willing to let her present. I wanted my work named, and I wanted to keep the contract.

evidenceFacts.claim: I was on a six-month contract; Mira controlled the deciding recommendation.
I had built the forecast over six weeks.
The deck title read “Mira’s forecast” on my desk display.
Yesterday Mira said, “Let me lead this one. I’ll mention your work.”
I carried my own printed summary to the meeting.
The director said, “Mira, this could become our board proposal.”
I recognized my previous-evening revision in the figures and had not heard my name so far.
A break preceded questions; I went to the hallway; Mira and the director stayed; the door was open.
During the break I could return and step out again; on resuming I could sit or stand nearer the director.
My name was at the top of my summary; below it was the same revision.
On resuming the director asked, “Anything to add before we use this?”
I could speak now, request private credit clarification later, or explicitly let this question pass.
I did not know if Mira would credit me later or how a challenge would affect her recommendation.
I accepted her presenting, wanted my work named, and wanted to keep the contract.

neutral: Shallow three-quarter office geometry with one unlettered table and open meeting threshold.
Anonymous adult figures; no additional meeting attendees, badges, career titles or likeness.
Initial Mira/director meeting marks allocate their later-view placement only; no offscreen action or earlier whereabouts are delivered as evidence while hero is at the desk.
Neutral paper/ink palette, practical overhead light and optional low office ventilation; no supplied time of day.

The named summary uses DOM text “My name” as an editorial representation; no fictional personal name or numerical forecast is added. The public slide shows only the sourced title plus non-readable figure texture.
forbidden: Night skyline, clock time, staring colleagues, Mira’s smirk, director sympathy, board approval, withheld recommendation letter.
stagingApproval.composition: Desk: display heading dominates hero’s sightline; summary is a carried edge, not a second task. Meeting: public display in back plane, Mira beside it, hero on table side and director reachable in hearing. Hallway: open jamb divides held summary from visible room. Return: matched table geometry, same actors; hero can sit or stand nearer director. At 390px use a desk insert and a threshold crop that preserves paper/jamb, never shrink the whole office.
stagingApproval.extra: A room visit during the break is a projection of c_meeting_before with a break-state overlay, not replay of its historical beats. It is not a fifth spine scene. After Resume, portals to the prior break close; the transcript remains. The desk is earlier time, never a reversible live portal.

revealSource.text:
I said, “I built the forecast, and I can explain the revision.” My voice shook.

I could accept not being the presenter. I couldn’t accept watching my work become hers in the board proposal.

Mira did not look at me. After the meeting she said I had embarrassed her. I kept the contract, but she stopped inviting me to preparation meetings. A month later, the director asked me to present the next update. I still don’t know whether speaking helped my contract or nearly cost it.
